references.text: Mentions Isaac's marriage to Rebekah, daughter of Bethuel the Aramean from Paddan-Aram and sister of Laban—the same family relationships described in Gen 28:5.
Describes Esau's hatred toward Jacob and Rebekah's plan to send Jacob to her brother Laban in Haran, which is the background for Isaac's sending in 28:5.
Isaac commands Jacob to go to Paddan-Aram, to Bethuel, Rebekah's father—the immediate context for the sending in verse 5.
Tells of Jacob's arrival with Laban in the east and their first meeting, which is the direct follow-up to the journey described in 28:5.
The verses are linked through Jacob's identity as Rebekah's son and Laban's nephew; 28:5 establishes the journey to this family, while 29:12 shows how he uses this kinship in his meeting with Rachel.
